geo_headlines: TRUMP PAUSED NEW IRAN STRIKES FRIDAY NIGHT — first pause in two weeks of continuous kinetic activity; White House framed it as giving negotiations time. Not a ceasefire. Iran still faces US 'much higher level' strike threat if talks collapse.

TRUMP TRUTH SOCIAL: US WILL HOLD IRAN RESPONSIBLE FOR ANY FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS — post-Thu tanker strikes, Trump declared 'major military punishment' would be inflicted on both Iran and Houthis if attacks recur. Set a de facto red line on Red Sea shipping.

HOUTHIS STRUCK SAUDI ARABIA SATURDAY — Iran-backed forces launched drones/missiles at Saudi in retaliation for Saudi strike on Hodeida Fri. First direct Houthi-Saudi kinetic exchange since 2022 ceasefire lapse. Bab el-Mandeb + Hormuz now BOTH active chokepoint risks.

IRAN CLAIMS DESTROYED 17 US DRONES, F-15 HANGAR, P-8, C-17 AT MIDEAST BASES — Revolutionary Guards claim significant material damage at US bases in Kuwait/Bahrain/Jordan; not independently verified. Four US KIA already in prior strike waves.

IRAN DEMANDS SAUDI-YEMEN TALKS RESTART — Foreign Ministry spokesman Ismail Baghaei said Saudi-Yemen conflict needs political solution, not military. Positioned Iran as mediator role even as US strikes continue — diplomatic overture on the sidelines.

US-SAUDI CIVIL NUCLEAR DEAL WRINKLE — Wed signing hit backlash; Trump added condition Fri that deal only proceeds if Saudi joins Abraham Accords. WH: 'If Saudis do not join Abraham Accords, the deal is off.' Complicates Saudi role in Iran talks.
US HOUSE VOTED WAR-POWERS REBUKE Fri — nonbinding but first since ceasefire breakdown; signals bipartisan patience thinning with kinetic activity absent Congressional authorization.

OIL CONTEXT — Brent settled Fri $96.78 (-3.88%) after Thu $100.69 spike (highest since May), on China/Pakistan peace-talk push. Weekly Brent +9.7%, WTI +8.3%. Physical supply risk in tact; positional length reduced going into weekend.

SETUP FOR MONDAY — massive earnings week (V/PYPL/SBUX Tue AC, MSFT+META Wed AC post-FOMC, AAPL+AMZN Thu AC). FOMC Wed 2pm ET with July FedWatch showing 7/29 hike odds shifted further hawkish to 38.5% (was 34.2% Fri, 24.6% Tue). GDP Q2 Thu, PCE Fri. Fed blackout continues through Tue.
headline: Weekend hold: Trump paused new Iran strikes Fri night (first pause in 2 weeks) but Houthi-Saudi kinetic exchange overnight Sat opened new chokepoint. FedWatch shifted further hawkish Sat report — 7/29 hike odds now 38.5%. Sun futures reopen 6pm ET into massive week.
client_frame: Sunday edition. No overnight tape churn — futures reopen at 6pm ET tonight — but the setup for the trading week is materially different from Friday morning. Three things shifted over the weekend, one of which is not obvious. First, Trump paused new Iran strikes Friday night, the first pause in two weeks of continuous kinetic activity. This is not a ceasefire; the White House framed it as giving diplomatic pathways time, and Trump retained the option of 'much higher level' strikes if talks collapse. Iran's foreign ministry pushed back into the space by demanding Saudi-Yemen talks restart, positioning Iran as a mediator even as US strikes continue. This is a real de-escalation of tempo but not a resolution — the underlying kinetic and shipping-lane risks remain. Second, the Houthi-Saudi exchange escalated overnight Saturday. After Saudi struck Hodeida on Friday, Houthis retaliated with drones and missiles into Saudi Arabia on Saturday — the first direct Houthi-Saudi kinetic exchange since the 2022 ceasefire lapse. Bab el-Mandeb (Red Sea) and Hormuz are now both active shipping chokepoint risks simultaneously. Trump posted on Truth Social Friday that any future Houthi attack would trigger 'major military punishment' on Iran, drawing a de facto red line on Red Sea shipping. That red line was tested within 24 hours. Third — and this is what the market will price Monday morning — the FedWatch cohort shifted further hawkish over the weekend. The July 29 meeting hike odds are now 38.5%, up from 34.2% on Friday's report and 24.6% on Tuesday. Cumulative +25bp into September is 80.9% priced. This is the rate market absorbing the oil shock alongside a Fed blackout that prevented any communication. That is the setup Powell walks into on Wednesday afternoon. The event stack for the week is denser than any I can remember: FOMC Wednesday 2pm ET plus Powell presser (Fed hasn't spoken publicly in 12 days), Microsoft and Meta after close Wednesday, GDP Q2 advance Thursday 8:30, Apple and Amazon after close Thursday, PCE deflator and Employment Cost Index Friday 8:30. Combined MSFT + META + AAPL + AMZN market cap of roughly $14 trillion reporting into a Fed meeting where the market is now debating whether Powell hikes into stagflation fears. After Alphabet got tattooed 7.3% Thursday for a $195-205B capex guide and Tesla 8.2% for 1.4% operating margin, the guidance discipline of the remaining mega-caps will be scrutinized with much less benefit of the doubt than in prior quarters. Intel's Thursday-night blowout — $16.13B revenue versus $14.43B consensus, Data Center +59% — is the counter-example the bulls will hold onto: capex is not automatically margin destruction if revenue and mix ratify it. That will be the frame for MSFT and AAPL Wednesday. Positioning framing for the week: the risk stool remains three-legged — Big Tech capex fatigue on the largest names, Iran/oil channel now with dual chokepoints, and Fed hawkish drift into a decision with no forward guidance runway. The asymmetry is Wednesday. If Powell threads the needle on inflation-versus-growth (says 'closely watching' but not 'imminently acting'), and MSFT and META guide clean capex with revenue attach, that is a squeeze setup. If Powell hints at 'restrictive setting warranted' language or either mega-cap disappoints on capex ratio, we get a fast trip to test S&P 7,400 and possibly 7,300. Do not add fresh equity risk before Wednesday. Hedges from Thursday paid; keep them on through the FOMC and the mega-cap prints. If the Sunday 6pm ET futures open shows a meaningful gap either direction, that's the tell for whether the weekend digestion was risk-on (Trump pause) or risk-off (Houthi-Saudi exchange, FedWatch hawkish drift).
